description: Conservative SecHub Resources SC4S pack for Cisco ASA/FTD legacy syslog messages. Extends upstream SC4S Cisco ASA inventory with public-example grounded fixtures, strict token routing, non-lossy Splunk field extraction, and no lab-validation statement.

normalized_fields.cisco_facility: ASA or FTD facility prefix extracted from %ASA/%FTD syslog messages for product-family/source-mode triage
normalized_fields.cisco_severity: raw Cisco numeric severity token (0-7) extracted from fixture-backed %ASA/%FTD prefixes before severity_label mapping
normalized_fields.cisco_msg_id: raw Cisco ASA/FTD message identifier extracted from fixture-backed %ASA/%FTD prefixes and used as signature/signature_id
normalized_fields.cisco_message: raw Cisco ASA/FTD message body preserved after the %ASA/%FTD prefix extraction for parser-audit and troubleshooting context
normalized_fields.src_ip: source IP extracted from fixture-backed ASA connection/deny payloads when present
normalized_fields.src_interface: source ASA interface extracted from fixture-backed connection/deny payloads when present
normalized_fields.dest_ip: destination IP extracted from fixture-backed ASA connection/deny payloads when present
normalized_fields.dest_interface: destination ASA interface extracted from fixture-backed connection/deny payloads when present
normalized_fields.connection_id: connection identifier extracted from fixture-backed ASA connection messages when present
normalized_fields.transport: uppercase protocol token normalized from fixture-backed ASA message text when present
normalized_fields.direction: inbound/outbound direction token from fixture-backed connection messages when present
normalized_fields.action: normalized analyst action: blocked for Deny, allowed for Built connection/translation, teardown for Teardown; vendor_raw_action preserves Cisco verb
normalized_fields.vendor_raw_action: raw Cisco ASA message verb such as Built, Teardown, or Deny preserved from fixture-backed payloads before any future analyst normalization
normalized_fields.nat_original_interface: ASA interface for the original side of fixture-backed dynamic translation messages when present
normalized_fields.nat_original_ip: Original endpoint IP from fixture-backed dynamic translation messages when present
normalized_fields.nat_original_port: Original endpoint port from fixture-backed dynamic translation messages when present
normalized_fields.nat_translated_interface: ASA interface for the translated side of fixture-backed dynamic translation messages when present
normalized_fields.nat_translated_ip: Translated endpoint IP from fixture-backed dynamic translation messages when present
normalized_fields.nat_translated_port: Translated endpoint port from fixture-backed dynamic translation messages when present

supported_transports.label: TCP syslog
supported_transports.notes: Dedicated SecHub Resources TCP listener for lab/onboarding; upstream SC4S documentation recommends TCP/IP for ASA logging.

supported_transports.label: UDP syslog
supported_transports.notes: Legacy ASA deployments often use UDP/514; documented only as a deployment consideration here because this pack currently ships a TCP listener/replay artifact only.

supported_transports.label: TLS syslog RFC5425
supported_transports.notes: Optional hardened transport for capable deployments; documented only as a deployment consideration here because this pack currently ships a TCP listener/replay artifact only.

source_log_version.name: Cisco ASA/FTD syslog message IDs
source_log_version.notes: Grounded in upstream SC4S Cisco ASA documentation, upstream lite parser matching %ASA/%FTD messages, and public Filebeat Cisco ASA sample events. Exact ASA/FTD release coverage needs device replay.

validation.source_log_version: Upstream SC4S Cisco ASA docs/parser inventory plus public Filebeat ASA example-event shapes; synthetic-equivalent fixtures only
validation.evidence: Public evidence confirms %ASA/%FTD message routing and example message shapes for connection/translation events. Live ASA/FTD replay and Splunk read-back evidence is not yet captured; keep quality_status=curated and trust_level=unverified.

required_splunk_capabilities: HEC or SC4S HEC path can write to netfw

readback.spl: index=netfw sechub_fixture_marker="SC4S_CISCO_ASA_TEST_*" earliest=-2h | table _time index sourcetype source host vendor product vendor_product cisco_facility cisco_severity severity_label cisco_msg_id cisco_message signature signature_id connection_id action vendor_raw_action direction transport src src_interface src_ip src_port dest dest_interface dest_ip dest_port nat_original_interface nat_original_ip nat_original_port nat_translated_interface nat_translated_ip nat_translated_port duration bytes icmp_type icmp_code access_group eventtype _raw

last_attempt.summary: 2026-06-07 local preflight found no TCP listener on 127.0.0.1:20042: ss returned only the header row and bash /dev/tcp returned connection refused. Local Splunk TEST reachability was also blocked because 127.0.0.1:8089 and 127.0.0.1:8000 refused TCP connections. Fixture replay, SC4S/syslog-ng counter checks, HEC delivery, and Splunk indexed read-back were not run.

evidence.summary: Command-grounded local preflight evidence for the missing Cisco ASA TCP listener and unavailable local Splunk TEST ports; not replay/read-back validation.
Splunk TEST dashboard XML and fixture-backed panel SPL validation only; not full SC4S listener/HEC/source validation.

timestamp_policy.primary_timezone: Fixture timestamps include a year but no timezone; configure source timezone in Splunk/SC4S for production read-back
timestamp_policy.notes: Fixtures use ASA-style syslog timestamps with month/day/year/time and no timezone; production deployments must define source timezone handling.

field_delimiting.escape_policy: Fixtures use documentation IP ranges and synthetic hostnames while preserving Cisco ASA message grammar.
field_delimiting.notes: Connection examples are intentionally narrow smoke fixtures, not a complete ASA message catalog.

source.reference: Upstream SC4S Cisco ASA docs and lite parser, Cisco product logging configuration guide, and Elastic Filebeat Cisco ASA public test logs used as event-shape evidence.
source.notes: Fixtures are synthetic-equivalent and use RFC5737 documentation IP ranges plus example hostnames. No customer samples or proprietary Splunk TA content are included.

curation.notes: Selected as a high-value firewall/security source absent from curated packs, with upstream SC4S inventory and public sample-message evidence. Conservative curation only; no validation statement.

src.notes: Connection examples expose source interface/IP/port where extraction patterns match.

src_port.notes: Available for connection, translation, and TCP/UDP access-group deny messages when the ASA payload carries endpoint ports. ICMP denies may legitimately omit ports.

dest.notes: Destination endpoint from ASA connection/translation messages.

connection_id.notes: Extracted from fixture-backed ASA built/teardown connection messages where the payload carries a numeric connection identifier.

transport.notes: Protocol text such as TCP/UDP when present in message text.

direction.notes: Fixture-backed connection examples expose inbound/outbound direction tokens for built connection messages; translation, teardown, and deny messages may omit direction.

duration.notes: Available for teardown messages that include an ASA duration token such as 0:00:10.

bytes.notes: Available for teardown messages that include total bytes.

action.notes: Normalized conservatively from raw Cisco verbs: Deny -> blocked, Built -> allowed, Teardown -> teardown; vendor_raw_action preserves the exact Cisco token.

access_group.notes: Extracted from ASA access-group deny messages such as message ID 106023 when present.

icmp_type.notes: Extracted from ICMP access-group deny messages when the ASA payload includes type/code details.

icmp_code.notes: Extracted from ICMP access-group deny messages when the ASA payload includes type/code details.

signature.notes: Cisco message ID is a stable analyst signature for rule/search grouping.

cisco_facility.notes: Raw %ASA/%FTD prefix family preserved for source-mode triage; this does not state full Firepower feature coverage.

cisco_message.notes: Raw Cisco ASA/FTD message body preserved after header extraction so replay read-back can prove analyst fields remain traceable to the vendor payload.

severity.notes: Numeric Cisco severity from %ASA-nnn prefix plus a fixture-backed analyst-friendly severity_label mapping.

nat_original_ip.notes: Original endpoint IP from fixture-backed dynamic translation messages; kept separate from connection src/dest to avoid treating NAT mappings as flows.

nat_translated_ip.notes: Translated endpoint IP from fixture-backed dynamic translation messages; kept separate from connection src/dest to avoid treating NAT mappings as flows.

cim.notes: Network Traffic mapping is partial and currently grounded in a small set of ASA connection/translation examples.

src_endpoint.port.notes: Direct source port when extracted from TCP/UDP connection, translation, or deny payloads.

src_endpoint.interface_name.notes: Fixture-backed ASA ingress/source interface token such as inside or outside when the message grammar exposes it; not inferred when absent.

dst_endpoint.port.notes: Direct destination port when extracted from TCP/UDP connection, translation, or deny payloads.

dst_endpoint.interface_name.notes: Fixture-backed ASA egress/destination interface token such as inside or outside when the message grammar exposes it; not inferred when absent.

activity_name.notes: Uses normalized action plus vendor_raw_action/cisco_msg_id for known connection, translation, and deny verbs only.

firewall_rule.name.notes: Mapped only for fixture-backed access-group deny messages where ASA exposes the rule/access-group name.

metadata.uid.notes: Best-effort per-connection identifier for fixture-backed ASA connection messages; not available for every ASA message family.

metadata.product.feature.name.notes: Non-standard helper mapping for the raw ASA/FTD prefix family used to separate classic ASA from narrow FTD-prefixed smoke fixtures.

metadata.original_event.notes: Best-effort pointer to the preserved ASA/FTD message body after the syslog header; included for read-back auditability, not complete raw-event normalization.

traffic.bytes.notes: Mapped only when ASA teardown messages expose a total byte count.

connection_info.protocol_name.notes: Fixture-backed ASA protocol token such as TCP, UDP, or ICMP when extracted from connection or deny message text.

traffic_direction.notes: Best-effort mapping of explicit ASA inbound/outbound connection text only; not inferred for messages that omit a direction token.

severity.notes: Numeric Cisco severity and the fixture-backed severity_label mapping from the %ASA/%FTD prefix; not a full product severity taxonomy.

icmp.type.notes: Fixture-backed ASA ICMP access-group deny type value when the payload includes explicit type/code details; absent for TCP/UDP denies and connection events.

icmp.code.notes: Fixture-backed ASA ICMP access-group deny code value when the payload includes explicit type/code details; not inferred when omitted.

observer.ingress.interface.name.notes: ASA source interface token from fixture-backed connection/translation/deny messages; deployments should confirm interface perspective during live replay.

observer.egress.interface.name.notes: ASA destination interface token from fixture-backed connection/translation/deny messages; deployments should confirm interface perspective during live replay.

event.action.notes: Normalized action derived from vendor_raw_action; vendor_raw_action retains the raw Cisco verb before normalization.

rule.name.notes: Mapped only for fixture-backed access-group deny messages where ASA exposes the rule/access-group name.

event.id.notes: Best-effort ASA connection identifier when extracted from fixture-backed connection messages; not a global event identifier.

cisco.facility.notes: Vendor/pack-scoped raw %ASA/%FTD facility prefix for analyst triage; retained separately from vendor/product.

message.notes: Preserved Cisco ASA/FTD payload body after %ASA/%FTD header extraction for reviewer/audit context.

network.transport.notes: Fixture-backed ASA protocol token such as TCP, UDP, or ICMP when extracted from connection or deny message text.

network.direction.notes: Direct mapping of explicit ASA inbound/outbound connection tokens; absent where the payload does not carry direction.

log.level.notes: Fixture-backed mapping of Cisco numeric severity 0-7 to emergency/alert/critical/error/warning/notice/informational/debug.

network.bytes.notes: Mapped only when ASA teardown messages expose a total byte count.

icmp.type.notes: Preserves explicit ASA ICMP type from fixture-backed access-group deny payloads only.

icmp.code.notes: Preserves explicit ASA ICMP code from fixture-backed access-group deny payloads only.

nat.original.ip.notes: Original IP from fixture-backed dynamic translation messages only; not inferred for connection flows.

nat.translated.ip.notes: Translated IP from fixture-backed dynamic translation messages only; not inferred for connection flows.

logging_presets.label: Basic Cisco ASA ingestion
logging_presets.description: Parser, listener env example, fixtures, and minimal Splunk props. No drops or reductions.

logging_presets.label: Standard Cisco ASA firewall knowledge
logging_presets.description: Adds eventtypes and tags for common network/firewall searches, including product-family cisco/asa discovery tags, connection build/teardown groupings that exclude NAT translations and access-group denies, fixture-backed teardown duration/byte metric searches, dynamic translation discovery, access-group deny, fixture-backed ICMP deny facets, and the narrow %FTD-6-302015 UDP connection smoke fixture. No drops or reductions.

known_limitations: Not validated until real Cisco ASA/FTD records are replayed through SC4S and read back from Splunk.
Fixture coverage is limited to common connection/translation/TCP deny/ICMP deny and narrow FTD UDP connection message shapes and does not cover the full Cisco ASA/FTD syslog catalog.
Fixture timestamps include a year but no timezone; production deployments must configure source timezone handling and confirm timestamp read-back.
No default reduction/drop rules are included.

source_delivery.notes: ASA/FTD syslog can be sent directly or through a relay to SC4S.
source_delivery.validation_status: metadata_classification_only; does not imply live replay/read-back validation
